verdict: OK to lend in Jamnagar brass — back registered foundries and machining units with metal-price pass-through and tested buyers; skip unregistered job-work shops and anyone funding inventory with short bank lines.
title: Jamnagar Non-ferrous Metals, Brass & Fabricated Metal: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Jamnagar is India's main brass-components cluster: about 3,500 units per the BEE profile — 900 foundries, 150 extrusion, 2,100 machining, 350 electroplating — with a state estimate of nearly 8,000 units of all sizes and 3 lakh+ jobs [1].** A part moves through several firms: ingot or rod is cast or extruded, then turned, milled, threaded, drilled and plated, in GIDC Phases I and II, Patel Colony, M.P. Shah, Hapa and Digvijay Plot [1]. Products run from one gram to ten kilograms, sold to electrical, plumbing, Railways and defence buyers [1]. So when a proposal lands, check which step of the chain the borrower actually owns; a machining shop with no furnace has a very different asset base from a foundry.

## Where cash and value sit
**Copper and zinc scrap and ingots are most of a part's cost, and volatile metal prices are the cluster's main challenge [1].** That means the borrower's real margin is conversion — melting, machining, plating — not metal. Ask for the conversion charge per kilogram separately from metal cost; if the customer cannot show it, collect from customer. Working capital is metal inventory plus receivables from larger OEM buyers; capex is furnaces, blowers and machine tools, which is why BEE runs energy-efficiency programmes here [1]. **Peer evidence says working capital is the pressure point: average utilisation of fund-based limits stayed high at 88% for the trailing twelve months at one metals borrower [8], and another carries moderately high working-capital needs supported by bank lines [9].**

## What has changed now
**The data call is OK (score 88; national 96, Gujarat 75) [D].** Gujarat GST collections are up 11.9% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and India-wide NIC 25 output is up 16.9% YoY, 12.0% Apr-to-date, with bank credit growth of 11.9% roughly matching output [D]. **Locally, scrap rates for brass and aluminium are sliding before Diwali even as global metal prices hold, on a festive lull [2] — that is a margin and inventory-valuation event, not a demand collapse.** Peer results are mixed: Gravita's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38% with EBITDA margin above 10% but PAT up only 6% [3][5], while KSH International's Q3 FY26 revenue rose 59% and PAT fell 9% [4]. Read that as volume growth without pricing power.

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue registered foundries and machining units with named electrical, plumbing or Railway buyers, conversion-charge pricing and a tested metal-pricing clause; avoid unregistered job-work shops and pure traders holding metal on short bank lines.** Gujarat has declared brass parts a cluster industry and priority sector under Atmanirbhar Gujarat 2022, with SIDBI support for finance and quality control [1] — use that for testing and certification, which export buyers demand [1]. Structure limits against inventory plus receivables, take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, and require the borrower to pass metal-price moves to customers.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch limit utilisation above 88% [8], falling conversion charges, and inventory valued at pre-Diwali scrap rates [2].** If a borrower's receivable days stretch while metal prices slide, ask for the buyer-wise ageing and the pricing clause.
